key_insight: An open-source nnUNet v2 model can automatically segment cerebral arteries on 3D rotational angiography with strong agreement to expert annotations and clinically usable results.
clinical_relevance: This could speed up endovascular planning and cerebrovascular research by reducing the time and variability of manual artery segmentation.
method: Trained on 400 consecutive 3DRA scans from three angiographic systems.
Compared four nnUNet v2 configurations and loss functions, then prospectively validated the best model on 40 patients.
Evaluated performance with quantitative metrics plus blinded expert ratings of 12 arterial segments and overall clinical usability.
evidence_signal: In prospective testing, the ensemble achieved median DSC 0.917, clDice 0.932, and HD95 1.494 mm, with clinical usability judged acceptable in 88–90% of cases.
watch_item: Performance was weaker in distal arterial segments, so real-world deployment may still need expert review for fine distal detail.
paper_title: Automated Segmentation of Cerebral Arteries on Three-Dimensional Rotational Angiography Using nnUNet v2: Prospective Validation with Quantitative Metrics and Expert Qualitative Assessment
